# A single isolatable simplex facet pays from own section-centroid data

This isolates the exact useful part of the archived simplex neutrality
theorem. Full affine freedom of the source is unnecessary once actual
cap stationarity has already supplied the section centroids and the
actual response balance. The discovery and planar formula were supplied
by the contributor and independently checked here.

## 1. Exact hypotheses

Let T be a d-simplex with vertices v_0,...,v_d and volume V. Let y have
positive barycentric coordinates y_i. Suppose there are d+1 actual caps,
one strictly isolating each vertex, whose own sections all have centroid y.
Assume their continuous normals span dimension d and their ACTUAL
response weights theta_i>0 satisfy sum theta_i=1 and

    sum_i theta_i S_i u_i=0,

where S_i is their own section coarea in the same normal normalization.
This follows from the full response balance whenever all actual section
coarea lies in this one source fiber. It can also be imposed directly;
one must not substitute own coarea for a different global coarea.

For positive-width problems the following statements are exact at a
retained h=0 limit with these properties. A small-width consequence
requires actual convergence of its marks, menus, and facet profiles.

## 2. Each facet has the SAME weighted constant-test capture

Section-centroid geometry gives the edge intercepts of vertex-i cap:

    t_ij=d y_j, j!=i.

Put r_i=1-d y_i. Minimal positive normal balance excludes zero intercept
degeneracies exactly as in Section3 of the archived source cited below,
so r_i>0 and sum r_i=1. The own cap volume fractions are

    q_i=d^d product_j y_j/y_i.

Either the pyramid/coarea formula or differentiation of these own cap
fractions gives the actual response weights

    theta_i=(r_i/q_i)/B,     B=sum_j r_j/q_j.           (1)

For completeness, the gradients of q_i in barycentric coordinates have
components q_i/y_j for j!=i and0 for j=i. Response balance says the sum
of these gradients is constant on the coordinate-sum-one affine plane.
Writing T0=sum theta_i q_i gives theta_i q_i=T0(1-d y_i)=T0 r_i.
Normalizing theta gives T0=1/B, proving (1).

On the facet F_i opposite vertex i, cap i has zero facet measure. For
j!=i the cap cuts the facet simplex in a vertex cap of relative area

    q_j/(d y_i).

Therefore the UNIFORM-FACET average of the actual weighted profile is

    sum_(j!=i) theta_j q_j/(d y_i)
       =(1-r_i)/(B d y_i)=1/B,                        (2)

independently of i. This is an exact boundary capture identity, not a
comparison of an arbitrary boundary weight to volume depth.

The algebraic constant is

    1/B = product_i(1-r_i)/(1-sum_i r_i^2) >= Gamma_d. (3)

The sharp inequality and its equality case were already proved in
`candidate 19aecfceb071d1da`,
Section5. Briefly, for log of this ratio, the difference of its i,j
partial derivatives has the sign of r_i-r_j, since its positive-denominator
numerator is (sum_(k!=i,j) r_k)^2+sum_(k!=i,j)r_k^2. Pairwise averaging
therefore decreases the ratio to its uniform value Gamma_d. For d>=2
equality occurs only at uniform r; d=1 gives1/2 identically.

## 3. One ENTIRE isolatable facet is sufficient

Suppose one actual admissible nonnegative convex physical field has
boundary restriction equal to a positive constant on one entire own
facet F_i and zero on every other measured boundary part. Equations
(2)--(3) show that this field pays at least Gamma_d for the actual menu.
No isolation of the full projective cone is needed. A partially free
facet does not automatically suffice: the constant-test identity uses
the entire facet and cannot be restricted to an arbitrary subset.

## 4. Exact application to the anchored tiny-triangle family

In the family from
`candidate 6df920a6fc1694e9`,
put alpha=sigma^2. Every active finite-width section is in the middle
triangle only. In any limit h->0 the own normal stationarity gives all
three section centroids equal to the source y. The symmetry exchanging
B and C fixes its barycentrics as (1-2t,t,t). There is one uniquely
determined section-centroid cap per vertex at this y. Their outside masses
are alpha V for the A cap and0 for the B,C caps. Common raw cap budget
therefore gives

    4t^2+alpha=4t(1-2t),
    t=(1+sqrt(1-3alpha))/6<1/3.                        (4)

The branch near1/3 is forced by the already certified source-core bounds.
The response weights are exactly

    theta_A=(4t-1)/(6t-1),
    theta_B=theta_C=t/(6t-1).

On the free facet opposite A, the B and C cap-length fractions both equal
2t. Its weighted constant-test efficiency is consequently

    4t^2/(6t-1)
      =4/9 + 4(3t-1)^2/[9(6t-1)] > Gamma_2.           (5)

That ENTIRE facet is actually isolatable. It is x1=-1, while both endpoint
triangles have x1>=c:=2-3sigma. Take a nonnegative continuous normal bump
chi, equal1 at its outer normal -e1 and zero at the two other triangle
facet normals, and use

    Phi(n,z,x)=chi(n)[c-x1]_+.

For each fixed normal this is convex in the full physical coordinates.
On the measured boundary it is exactly the constant c+1 on the middle
facet opposite A and zero elsewhere. Thus it realizes (5) as an actual
physical-field efficiency, despite the failure of full own-cone isolation.

All actual h>0 active normals were already confined to three compact
cones. Their own-strip centroid equations pass to the uniquely determined
caps in (4), so the response measures and this facet capture converge.
For fixed sigma>0, the strict margin in (5) therefore persists for all
sufficiently small positive h. No uniform h threshold of order sigma^2
is claimed: the strict margin is of order alpha^2=sigma^4. The earlier
all-menu obstructions hold on a much larger width range, and should not
be confused with this smaller-width strict-payment conclusion.

This pays the concrete diagnostic family. In a general simplex source
the unresolved requirements remain own-only coarea, the one-cap-per-
vertex incidence, and an ENTIRE isolatable facet.
